title: The Principle of Quantum Superposition
text:
Quantum mechanics posits that subatomic particles do not possess definite properties until an observation is made. Before measurement, a particle exists in a state of superposition, meaning it simultaneously inhabits all possible states allowed by its wave function.

The act of measuring the system causes this superposition to collapse instantaneously into a single, defined eigenvalue. This mechanism distinguishes quantum behavior sharply from classical physics, where particles are assumed to follow predictable trajectories regardless of observation.

Understanding this relationship between potentiality (superposition) and actuality (measurement) is central to modern theoretical physics, suggesting that physical reality itself may be fundamentally probabilistic.
